subject: Post-call: DPA clarifications + retention & breach notice
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@cardinalht.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@cardinalht.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call: DPA clarifications + retention & breach notice
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (application/pdf), subprocessors_20260210.csv (text/csv)

Hi Sara / Alex —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Quick recap and a set of specific items we said we'd follow up on so your Legal/InfoSec can review: 

- Roles: Confirming Cardinal HealthTech intends Redwood to act as Processor and Cardinal as Controller for the workload we discussed. Please confirm if that is correct for all data flows.
- Retention: You mentioned needing longer-term retention for PII (medical claims) — what retention window are you targeting (e.g., 7 years)? We can document configurable retention but want to make sure we capture the exact requirement.
- Breach notice SLA: You asked about timing for incident notification. Our standard DPA language is 72 hours for a substantive incident report; can you confirm if your requirement is 48 hours initial notification or 48 hours full report?
- Subprocessors & SOC2: Per call, attaching our current subprocessor list CSV and the draft DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf). Please let us know if you require SOC 2 Type II evidence or any additional audit materials up front — we can provide current reports under NDA.
- Data residency: You indicated US-only residency for this dataset. Can you confirm the region(s) and whether multi-region failover is acceptable (we can restrict primary storage to us-east-1 or a specific region)?
- Logging & access: You requested 90 days of immutable audit logs and exportability. Our platform keeps detailed audit logs by default; we usually retain 90 days in the hosted plan and can extend with an add-on. Any additional retention or retention-on-export needs?
- Pseudonymization / field redaction: You asked about SSN/PHI handling. We offer field-level redaction and client-side pseudonymization patterns (SE can provide implementation guidance).

Next steps I propose:
1) Sara, please confirm Controller/Processor model and retention window.
2) Legal: flag any required DPA edits — we'll iterate on the draft.
3) Security: Vivek / Stephanie, can you validate the feasibility of 48-hour vs 72-hour breach notice and confirm what artifacts we can supply (SOC2, penetration test summaries, subprocessors)?
4) Marissa/Procurement: Once Legal confirms, I will circulate the DocuSign draft (linked) and set up a short follow-up with your team.

Thanks — aiming to have a revised DPA and answers back by EOD Wednesday next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

--
Original meeting notes attached in the DPA for context.

From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@cardinalht.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cardinalht.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:28:42 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA clarifications + retention & breach notice

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few answers to get us started: 

- Roles: Confirmed — Cardinal HealthTech will be Controller; Redwood Inference will be Processor for the workloads discussed.
- Retention: For the subset of PII tied to claims we need a 7-year retention for regulatory reasons. For derived embeddings/metadata we would like to minimize retention where possible; we can provide a table mapping classes to retention windows.
- Breach notice: We require an initial notification within 48 hours of detection for incidents affecting PII, with a follow-up full report within 10 business days. If 48 hours is not standard for you, please propose alternative language.
- Subprocessors / audits: We will need the current subprocessor list and SOC 2 Type II report; also any SAP or penetration test summaries you can share.
- Data residency: US-only for primary storage and processing. Multi-region failover is acceptable if data-at-rest remains in the US and replication is within approved regions — we'll provide network boundary requirements in our security questionnaire.
- Logging: 90 days of immutable, exportable audit logs is required. In addition, we want the ability to pull user-level access logs for specific principals on demand for eDiscovery.
- Pseudonymization: We would prefer server-side field-level redaction for SSNs and explicit support for hashing/pseudonymization of patient identifiers if possible; please indicate whether that is a built-in feature or requires integration.

Please route technical details and the redline DPA to my legal and security colleagues (cc'd above if needed). For procurement, include our SOW contact and we can align timelines.

Appreciate the quick follow-up.

Best,
Sara Lewis
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Cardinal HealthTech
sara.lewis@cardinalht.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 17:05:10 -0500
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call: DPA clarifications + retention & breach notice

Folks — forwarding Sara's note from Cardinal HealthTech. Highlights they want: controller confirmed, 7-year retention for PII, 48-hour initial breach notice, SOC2 + pen test artifacts, US-only residency, 90-day immutable logs, server-side redaction/pseudonymization for SSNs.

Quick asks: 
- Rishi: take a look at the DPA draft attached and flag any legal blockers for committing to 48-hour initial notice vs our standard 72h.
- Vivek: can we commit to 48-hour initial notice? If not, can we propose a compromise (e.g., initial notification within 48 hours for incidents with confirmed data exfil and 72h for suspected incidents)? Also please confirm what artifacts we can share (SOC2 type II, pentest summary).
- Stephanie: can you comment on technical support for server-side field redaction/pseudonymization and audit log exportability (90 days immutable).

Would like to get a consolidated response to Sara by EOD tomorrow so they can move legal/procurement.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Post-call: DPA clarifications + retention & breach notice

Marissa — quick responses inline below. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through.

- Breach notice timing: Our standard commitment in the hosted DPA is 72 hours for a substantive report. Operationally we can provide an initial acknowledgement/alert within 48 hours for confirmed incidents involving PII (high confidence) and follow-up with a fuller technical report within 72 hours. We can propose phrasing: "Initial notification within 48 hours for incidents confirmed to have impacted PII; full incident report within 72 hours of confirmation." Rishi please review for legal viability.

- SOC2 / artifacts: We can provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and a redacted penetration test summary. Subprocessor list (attached by Marissa) is current — we can supply an export and a short explanation of each provider's role.

- Data residency: We can ensure primary processing and at-rest storage in us-east-1 (or another US region). Failover that keeps data within the US is doable with the right configuration. Stephanie can map the region options.

- Logging & retention: Default audit log retention for hosted customers is 90 days immutable. We can offer extended retention (365 days or custom) as a paid add-on; logs are exportable via S3 export or API and can be scoped to principals for eDiscovery use cases.

- Field redaction / pseudonymization: Out-of-the-box we offer configurable redaction rules that can scrub or hash defined fields at ingestion. For SSN-specific automatic detection we recommend a hybrid: customer-supplied field markers or a preprocessing step to tokenise SSNs before sending. We can scope professional services to automate this mapping if they want server-side detection.

Next steps we recommend: we (Legal + Security + SE) produce a one-page response capturing commitments and any optional paid add-ons (extended logs, long-term retention, PS for redaction). I'll coordinate with Stephanie to include the technical approach and with Rishi for the DPA language.

-Vivek
Director of Security, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
